title: Halide ions
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AQA A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: PT06#t4 term and clue written for the game; PT06#t1 term and clue written for the game; PT06#t2 term and clue written for the game; PT06#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: PT06#N.3, PT06#N.5, PT06#N.10, PT06#N.14.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Precipitate
items.clue: Insoluble product, such as AgX(s), that appears when Ag⁺(aq) meets X⁻(aq).

items.label: Silver nitrate
items.clue: Solution added after acidifying; gives a white, cream or yellow solid with a halide.

items.label: Nitric acid
items.clue: Added first, dilute, to remove carbonate and hydroxide without adding Cl⁻ or sulfate.

items.label: Ammonia solution
items.clue: Added last to confirm the halide: AgCl dissolves when it is dilute, AgBr only when it is concentrated.

questions.stem: A student tests a solution for halide ions by adding silver nitrate solution acidified with dilute hydrochloric acid. A white precipitate forms. What can the student conclude?

options.text: The solution contains chloride ions, because AgCl is white.
The solution contains carbonate ions, because the acid did not remove them.
The solution contains no bromide or iodide, because the precipitate is not cream or yellow.
Nothing about chloride ions, because the hydrochloric acid itself added Cl⁻ ions.

questions.explanation: Right. The added Cl⁻ forms white AgCl whatever was in the sample. Repeat with dilute nitric acid.

questions.stem: An unknown sodium halide solution is acidified and silver nitrate is added. The precipitate does not dissolve in dilute ammonia solution, but does dissolve in concentrated ammonia solution. Which ion is present?
questions.explanation: AgBr (cream) dissolves only in concentrated ammonia. That matches both results.

questions.stem: Concentrated sulfuric acid is added separately to solid sodium bromide and to solid sodium iodide. Which product forms with sodium iodide but not with sodium bromide?
questions.explanation: Only iodide is a strong enough reducing agent to take sulfur from +6 all the way to −2 in H₂S (bad-egg smell).

questions.stem: A solution contains both potassium chloride and potassium iodide. Acidified silver nitrate is added until no more precipitate forms. Then excess concentrated ammonia solution is added and the mixture is shaken. What is seen at the end?

options.text: A white precipitate and a yellow precipitate both remain
A cream precipitate remains and the solution is colourless
No precipitate remains and the solution is colourless

questions.explanation: Both AgCl and AgI form. Ammonia dissolves the AgCl but not the AgI, so the yellow precipitate is left.
